verdicts.reason: A drops the Q logo entirely, jams the headline against the left edge and shrinks the can to a tiny icon wedged between headline and CTA. B keeps the logo, but it is a speck crammed between headline and sub-copy, the sub-copy is barely legible and the oversized CTA crowds the top-right edge. Still, the brand survives in B.

A is the same layout as pair 1 B: the logo is an illegible speck squeezed under the headline, the sub-copy is tiny and the CTA presses against the top edge. B reads cleanly from product to headline to CTA, but it drops the logo entirely and its CTA is undersized, which weakens the hierarchy. Losing the brand mark is the bigger failure.
